  ╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌
   Plan: add greet.sh

   Context

   Add a small shell script, greet.sh, to the probe worktree root that prints "hello".

   Steps

   1. Confirm the working directory is the probe worktree.
   2. Check that greet.sh does not already exist.
   3. Decide the script lives at the worktree root.
   4. Choose /bin/sh as the interpreter.
   5. Open a new file named greet.sh.
   6. Write the shebang line #!/bin/sh.
   7. Add a blank line after the shebang.
   8. Add the line echo hello.
   9. End the file with a trailing newline.
   10. Save the file.
   11. Confirm the file exists with ls.
   12. Confirm the contents are exactly two lines plus a blank.
   13. Check the shebang has no stray whitespace.                                                                     ↓
